title: One scorer for all headline metrics
description:
As an evaluation owner, I want every headline metric to come from one matching function, so that fixture Jest, `benchmark:run`, and any precision helper cannot disagree on the same packet.

## Current mess

- **`tests/eval/score.ts`**: per-layer finding bags, `identity.ts` matching, path normalize, union of exhaustive scopes per fixture+layer, data-items identity-only, optional `finding.layer` tags.
- **`tests/benchmark/precision.ts`**: exact `finding.key === annotation.subject.key`, no taxonomy aliases, no layer tags, different overlap helper. Still used by `corpus-precision.spec.ts`.
- **Public `dataparade-cli`**: leftover eval/score/identity copy. The next `cli-v*` rsync from the app monorepo does not update scanner, but humans will still run the wrong tree.
- **Plexus** `evaluate accuracy` / `evaluate_recall`: third client, was not runnable in the last pass (proxy/backend mode). If it comes back with yet another identity rule, we will have four numbers.

`scanRepoByManifestLayers` comments claim personal-data matching runs at most once; the body can call `collectPersonalDataFindings` three times (mentions, raw-hits, data-items). That is a runner bug adjacent to “one scorer” (same scan, one finding inventory).

## Why it blocks scanner work

A “fix” that greens `benchmark:run` and reds `precision.ts` (or the reverse) is not a fix. Agents will pick the number that supports the patch.

## Questions to answer

- Is `scoreEvalCases` the only matcher? Then `precision.ts` becomes a thin wrapper or dies.
- Does corpus CI call `run-benchmark` (materialize is opt-in) or only YAML load tests? What is the official command for headline numbers?
- After identity (task 1) and unread (task 2) land, which tests are the contract suite that must not be forked?
- Do we delete or archive eval code on `dataparade-cli` so it cannot rot into a second origin?

## Not this task

Do not add a fourth metrics pipeline (new notebooks, ad-hoc scripts) while this is open.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
## Decision

There is one canonical evaluator and one matching contract for every headline result. `scoreEvalCases` may remain the public entry point, but it must consume canonical observations from the shared adapters. `tests/benchmark/precision.ts` is deleted or reduced to a thin call into that evaluator; it may not own matching rules.

Matching is deterministic and cardinality-aware. The evaluator performs one-to-one assignment between expected observations and findings, preferring exact canonical identity and stronger evidence matches. One finding cannot satisfy several gold cases, and duplicate findings cannot all receive true-positive credit from one gold case. Unmatched evaluable positives are false negatives; unmatched findings in closed scope are false positives. Repository-level entity layers consolidate repeated evidence into one expected entity before assignment.

Closed-world scope is packet-and-layer metadata with review provenance, independent of positive annotations. This permits an exhaustively reviewed layer with zero positives to penalize hallucinated findings. Scope must not be stored only by repeating it on positive records.

The official headline path is the scanner repository command, accepted gold only, deterministic inference configuration with AI disabled, and validated pinned materializations. The contract suite includes synthetic golden inputs/outputs for identity, labels, eligibility, scope, one-to-one matching, duplicates, zero-positive scopes, and path normalization.

The public CLI and Plexus must call the shared evaluator through a library or stable JSON/process boundary. Copied scoring trees are removed or clearly archived as non-authoritative.

The adjacent runner defect is follow-on work: personal-data matching runs once per repo and the raw-hit, mention, and data-item projections derive from that one inventory.

Rejected alternatives:

- independent any-match loops for recall and precision;
- greedy order-dependent reuse of findings;
- separate corpus, Jest, CLI, or Plexus scorers;
- positive-attached scope as the only closed-world declaration;
- ad-hoc notebooks or scripts as headline sources.

Scorer implementation follows the identity, eligibility, and layer-unit decisions and must not retune detectors.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
_Review pass recorded before the contract decisions were posted; kept for provenance. Where it conflicts with a decision, the decision governs — the follow-up comment below reconciles the two._

## The divergence list is incomplete — four more, one of which silently deflates precision

Diffed `tests/eval/score.ts` against `tests/benchmark/precision.ts` line by line. Beyond exact-vs-alias and the different overlap helper:

**1. `precision.ts` unions exhaustive-scope files across *all layers* and pools *all findings* against them.**

`scoreCorpusPrecision` builds one `scopeFiles` set from every positive annotation regardless of layer, then walks every finding. `score.ts` buckets scope per `fixture::layer` via `scopeBucketKey`. Consequence: a mention finding located in a file that was scoped for the *components* layer enters the precision denominator and can never match a component annotation, so it counts as a false positive. Corpus precision from `precision.ts` is **structurally deflated**, not merely inconsistent. This one is worth treating as a bug independent of the contract decision.

**2. No path normalization.** `precision.ts` compares `evidence.file_path === sourceLine.file_path` and `scopeFiles.includes(filePath)` as raw strings. `score.ts` runs both sides through `normalizeEvalPath`. Any `./` prefix or backslash in gold silently drops the match.

**3. No `review_state` filter.** `precision.ts` filters `expected.status === "positive"` only, so it counts the **75 `proposed`** annotations as accepted gold, while `to-eval-cases.ts` defaults to `accepted` only. The two pipelines are scoring different corpora, not just scoring the same corpus differently.

**4. No layer tags.** `precision.ts` has no equivalent of `findingsForCaseLayer`, so a `data_item:email` finding can satisfy a `mentions` annotation with the same key.

### `documentedGap` cannot reach the corpus scorer at all

`annotationToEvalCase` constructs `expected` from `status` and `labels` only — `documentedGap` is never copied, and `AnnotationExpected` in `schema.ts` has no field for it. Independently, **0 of 1,792** annotations set any documented-gap flag. So both KDATAP-08a0ac and KDATAP-955d82 ask how documented gaps should appear in reports, and today there is no mechanism for them to appear through. Whatever this task decides about one scorer should include whether `documentedGap` is part of the corpus schema at all.

### The runner bug is real

`scanRepoByManifestLayers` carries the comment *"Orchestrator `scan()` runs at most once; personal-data matching at most once."* The body calls `collectPersonalDataFindings` up to three times (mentions, raw_hits, data_items), and each call runs its own `ingestFileSystem` + `matchPiiSignalsInFiles`. Same scan, three inventories. Fix belongs with "one finding inventory", agreed.

### The bigger version of "one scorer": there are two golds, not two scorers

This is the finding that most changes the task. Fixture Jest gold and corpus gold encode **different contracts**:

| | component keys | flow keys |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Jest fixtures (`tests/eval/layers/*/cases.ts`) | `asset:pg`, `asset:hikaricp`, `asset:psycopg2`, `third_party:stripe` — the **engine's** grammar | `flow:asset:api->third_party:stripe` — nested component keys |
| Corpus gold (29 packets) | `asset:database` x182, `asset:api` x118 — **taxonomy subtypes** | `flow:user->stripe`, `flow:password->wp_check_password` — bare prose |

Unifying on `scoreEvalCases` is necessary and not sufficient: one matcher over two incompatible vocabularies still produces two unrelated numbers. The Jest suite is green and will stay green through every change made here, so it cannot serve as the regression guard for this work. See KDATAP-08a0ac.

### Answers to the questions

- **Is `scoreEvalCases` the only matcher?** Recommend yes, and `precision.ts` dies rather than becoming a wrapper — `score.ts` already computes precision over per-layer scope buckets, so the wrapper would have no remaining logic. `corpus-precision.spec.ts` retargets.
- **Official command for headline numbers?** `pnpm run benchmark:run` (it is the only path that goes through `scoreEvalCasesByLayer`). Corpus CI should keep running the YAML load tests only; materializing 29 clones in CI is a separate call — see KDATAP-955d82.
- **Which tests are the contract suite?** After tasks 1 and 2: `tests/unit/eval/identity.spec.ts`, `tests/eval/score.test.ts`, `tests/unit/benchmark/corpus-gold.spec.ts`, plus whatever replaces `corpus-precision.spec.ts`. Recommend they be named as such in `tests/eval/README.md` so a future session knows what it is not allowed to fork.
- **Delete or archive the `dataparade-cli` eval copy?** Recommend delete. An archived copy that still runs is exactly how a second origin comes back.

Agreed on the boundary: no fourth pipeline while this is open.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
## The concrete bill for deleting `precision.ts`, and a caveat on the contract suite

### What `precision.ts` currently owns that the canonical evaluator must absorb

Diffed it against `score.ts`. Four divergences beyond exact-vs-alias, one of which is a live bug rather than an inconsistency:

1. **Scope unioned across layers.** `scoreCorpusPrecision` builds one `scopeFiles` set from every positive annotation regardless of layer, then walks every finding. `score.ts` buckets scope per `fixture::layer`. So a mention finding located in a file scoped for the components layer enters the precision denominator and can never match a component annotation — counted as a false positive. **Corpus precision is structurally deflated today.** Worth fixing as a bug even if the rewrite is weeks out, because any interim number cited from it is wrong in a known direction.
2. **No path normalization.** Raw string compare on `file_path` and `scopeFiles.includes()`, where `score.ts` runs both sides through `normalizeEvalPath`.
3. **No `review_state` filter.** It counts the **75 `proposed`** annotations as accepted gold, while `to-eval-cases.ts` defaults to `accepted` only. The two pipelines score different corpora, not just differently.
4. **No layer tags.** No equivalent of `findingsForCaseLayer`, so a `data_item:email` finding can satisfy a `mentions` annotation with the same key.

### One-to-one assignment fixes a measured problem

Confirming the cardinality defect is real and not theoretical. `IDENTITY_ONLY_LAYERS` makes `findingMatchesCase` return true for data items with no span check, and `findMatchingFinding` uses `.find()` — first match wins, no consumption. So one `data_item:email` finding satisfies every `data_item:email` gold case in the repo, in any file. With 436 data-item annotations across 29 packets and gold repeating keys within a packet, that is a direct recall inflator.

### Caveat: the fixture suite cannot be the regression guard for this work

The decision requires fixture Jest and corpus evaluation to pass through the same adapter and contract tests. Agreed — with the warning that **fixture gold is itself in a non-canonical vocabulary and must be migrated too**. It is not a fixed reference point:

| | component keys | flow keys |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Jest fixtures | `asset:pg`, `asset:hikaricp`, `asset:psycopg2` — the **engine's** instance names | `flow:asset:api->third_party:stripe` — nested component keys |
| Corpus gold | `asset:database` x182, `asset:api` x118 — **taxonomy subtypes** | `flow:password->wp_check_password` — bare prose |

The fixture suite is green today and will stay green through most of this migration, because it encodes the implementation being replaced. The synthetic golden inputs/outputs named in the decision are the right guard; the existing fixture cases are cargo until they are migrated.

### `documentedGap` — the reclassification resolves a dead end

Recording why it could not have worked as ground truth: `annotationToEvalCase` copies only `status` and `labels`, `AnnotationExpected` in `schema.ts` has no field for it, and **0 of 1,792** annotations set it. Moving it to release-gate policy is the right call. The gate-exception record (issue, owner, reason, expiry) will need a home in the corpus or baseline schema, since neither has one today.

### Scope as packet-and-layer metadata is a data migration

Supporting the zero-positive-scope decision with the current shape: scope exists only as `expected.exhaustive_scope_files` repeated across **434 positive annotations**, ~18.9k entries with heavy duplication. Relocating it to reviewed packet-and-layer metadata is a real migration with a dedup and review-provenance step, not a schema rename. It also removes the current failure where a layer reviewed exhaustively but containing no positives declares no scope at all and therefore cannot catch hallucinations — exactly the case the decision calls out.

### Runner defect confirmed

`scanRepoByManifestLayers` carries the comment "personal-data matching at most once" while the body calls `collectPersonalDataFindings` up to three times, each running its own `ingestFileSystem` + `matchPiiSignalsInFiles`. Agreed it is follow-on work; noting the comment is currently false so nobody reads it as a spec.
